entities.evidence: Genesis 5:25 identifies Lamech as Methuselah’s son, and Genesis 5:28–30 identifies him as Noah’s father. This verse closes his lifespan at 777 years.

analysis.evidence: The verb links כָּל יְמֵי לֶמֶךְ, “all the days of Lamech,” to the number of years that follows. Seventy-seven years plus seven hundred years gives his total lifespan of 777 years.
analysis.morphology: Qal wayyiqtol, third person masculine singular, with prefixed וַ־
analysis.sense: to amount to a stated total

analysis.evidence: כָּל יְמֵי לֶמֶךְ means “all the days of Lamech.” The verse gives their sum as 777 years, so כָּל refers to his lifespan as a whole.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular noun in the construct state.

analysis.evidence: כָּל יְמֵי לֶמֶךְ means “all the days of Lamech.” The verse totals those days as 777 years and closes with וַיָּמֹת, “and he died,” identifying them as his lifespan.
analysis.sense: (pl.) days of a life, a reign or an age

draft.change: Add a personal-name article for לֶמֶךְ with the derivation left open.
draft.definition: A Hebrew masculine personal name, borne here by the son of Methuselah.
draft.evidence: Genesis 5:25 names the child in וַיּוֹלֶד אֶת לָמֶךְ, “and he fathered Lamech.”

analysis.evidence: In כָּל יְמֵי לֶמֶךְ, “all the days of Lamech,” the name identifies whose lifespan totaled 777 years. Genesis 5:25 identifies this Lamech as Methuselah’s son.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular proper noun in the absolute state, without prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: In שֶׁבַע וְשִׁבְעִים שָׁנָה, “seven and seventy years,” the marked שֶׁבַע supplies the units digit of Lamech’s age of 777 years.
analysis.morphology: Feminine singular absolute cardinal numeral, without prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: In שֶׁבַע וְשִׁבְעִים שָׁנָה, the conjunction adds seventy to seven, giving seventy-seven years. The following seven hundred years bring Lamech’s lifespan to 777.
analysis.morphology: Conjunction וְ־ prefixed to a cardinal numeral, common gender, plural absolute.

analysis.evidence: In שֶׁבַע וְשִׁבְעִים שָׁנָה, the marked noun supplies the unit for seventy-seven. These years are added to seven hundred to give the lifespan introduced by כָּל יְמֵי לֶמֶךְ, “all the days of Lamech.”
analysis.morphology: Common noun, feminine singular absolute, with no prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: In וּשְׁבַע מֵאוֹת שָׁנָה ‘and seven hundred years’, שְׁבַע counts מֵאוֹת ‘hundreds’. This phrase contributes 700 to Lamech’s lifespan of 777 years.
analysis.morphology: Conjunction וּ־ ‘and’ prefixed to שְׁבַע, the feminine singular construct form of the cardinal numeral.

analysis.evidence: In וּשְׁבַע מֵאוֹת שָׁנָה, שֶׁבַע counts units of one hundred, giving “and seven hundred years.” Together with the preceding seventy-seven years, this gives Lamech’s lifespan of 777 years.
analysis.morphology: Cardinal numeral, plural absolute, without prefix or suffix.
analysis.sense: hundreds (plural מֵאוֹת, with the digits: three hundred to nine hundred)

analysis.evidence: In וּשְׁבַע מֵאוֹת שָׁנָה, “and seven hundred years,” the marked singular noun supplies the unit for the hundreds in Lamech’s total lifespan of 777 years. כָּל יְמֵי לֶמֶךְ, “all the days of Lamech,” identifies what is being counted.
After giving Lamech’s lifespan as 777 years, the verse concludes with וַיָּמֹת, reporting his death. The masculine singular verb refers to Lamech.
analysis.morphology: Qal wayyiqtol, third person masculine singular, with prefixed וַ־.
analysis.sense: die, come to the end of life
